title: AP Japanese Language and Culture
summary: Read Japanese notices and viewpoints, explain source limits and construct clear thematic responses.
frameworkNote: Checked against the revised 2026-27 framework on 15 October 2026: six thematic units and a course project supporting exam speaking tasks. The 2027 project packet is due for release in January 2027. These original fictional text scenarios are practice, not authentic cultural sources or a completed project. Add authentic target-language research, listening, conversation and teacher feedback; text answers do not assess pronunciation or oral proficiency.

modules.title: Extract details from a community notice
modules.focus: Families and communities: use particles for time, place and action.
explanation: Particles identify relationships. In “土曜日に公民館で会います”, に marks the scheduled time and で marks the place of the meeting: “We will meet at the community centre on Saturday.” A place where an action occurs usually takes で; existence statements such as “公民館にいます” use に.

A notice may omit the subject when it is clear from context. Read the deadline and participation condition before replying. The original fictional examples practise communication; they do not establish that every Japanese-speaking family takes part in the same activities.

workedExample.prompt: A notice says “金曜日までに申し込んでください。” Ask how to apply.
steps: Interpret までに as a deadline: apply by Friday.
Ask “どうやって申し込めばいいですか。” (How should I apply?)

misconception.claim: に and で are interchangeable whenever a place is named.
misconception.correction: Their roles differ: existence or destination and the location of an action are distinct relationships.

questions.prompt: Choose the particle: “図書館＿勉強します。”
questions.hint: Studying is an action at a location.
questions.answer: “図書館で勉強します。” (I study at the library.)

questions.prompt: What does “月曜日までに” mean?
questions.hint: The に makes a deadline expression.
checkpoints: Does not translate it as from Monday

modules.title: Read contrast and reported opinion
modules.focus: Language and culture: distinguish a source’s view from a fact.
explanation: “と思います” marks a thought or opinion, while “と言っています” reports what someone says. In “先生はこの表現が丁寧だと言っています”, the teacher is the source of the judgement that the expression is polite. Keep that attribution in a summary.

Register depends on situation and relationship. Polite forms can be appropriate in one exchange without proving social distance in every context. Analyse a particular interaction and avoid broad claims about national personality. Contrast markers such as しかし and でも help reveal how an argument qualifies its first point.

workedExample.prompt: Interpret “この言葉は短くて便利です。でも、正式なメールでは使いません。”
steps: Identify the benefit: the word is short and convenient.
Identify the restriction: the speaker does not use it in formal email. This is a contextual choice, not a claim that the word is always wrong.

misconception.claim: A reported opinion becomes an established fact.
misconception.correction: Attribution tells you whose judgement is being presented, not whether it has been independently verified.

questions.prompt: What does “便利だと思います” express?
questions.answer: The speaker thinks it is convenient.

questions.prompt: How would you report that a friend says a word is difficult?
questions.answer: “友達はこの言葉が難しいと言っています。”

modules.title: Connect music, action and meaning
modules.focus: Art and creativity: prepare an evidence-based research note.
explanation: A recording, instrument or written score can provide evidence about a musical product. Rehearsing or performing is a practice. A participant’s explanation of why they take part can support an interpretation of perspective. Keep those forms of evidence distinct and connected.

For authentic research, record a source’s creator, date, place and relevant passage or timestamp. Use actual Japanese-language sources and follow the official exam-year packet when available. The fictional statements here are language exercises and cannot serve as project evidence or assess listening and speaking proficiency.

workedExample.prompt: Read “地域の人と交流するために、毎月コンサートを開いています。”
steps: Identify the activity: holding a concert every month.
Explain the stated purpose: interacting with local people. ために marks purpose here.

misconception.claim: A concert’s musical style alone proves its social purpose.
misconception.correction: A purpose claim needs contextual evidence, such as participant testimony or documentation.

questions.prompt: What frequency is expressed by 毎月?
Paraphrase the stated aim in English.
questions.hint: Focus on 交流するために.
questions.answer: The organisers hold concerts to interact with people in the local community.
checkpoints: Does not invent a national custom

modules.title: Report a survey and its limits
modules.focus: Science and technology: separate measured data from possibility.
explanation: A percentage describes a defined group. “回答者の半分” means half of the respondents, not half of all residents. When reading a chart, check the number surveyed and whether people could choose more than one response.

“かもしれません” expresses possibility: “時間を節約できるかもしれません” means it may be possible to save time. This is weaker than claiming that a tool already saved time. A technology argument should name who benefits, who may lack access and what evidence would test the predicted effect.

workedExample.prompt: A fictional survey finds that 18 of 60 students use a timetable app.
steps: Report “回答した学生の30パーセントがこのアプリを使っています”, retaining the surveyed group.

misconception.claim: A survey of one class directly represents all students.
misconception.correction: A broader claim needs a justified sample and careful attention to the population.

questions.prompt: What does 半分 mean in a chart caption?

questions.answer: “便利かもしれません。” (It may be convenient.)

modules.title: Describe a change in everyday routine
modules.focus: Contemporary life: connect past experience and present habits.
explanation: “以前は” sets an earlier situation and “今は” contrasts the present. “以前は歩いて通学していましたが、今はバスで通っています” means the speaker used to walk to school but now travels by bus. The contrast is about this speaker, not every student.

Use temporal connectors to organise an account. “引っ越してから” means after moving, while “引っ越す前に” means before moving. The form before these expressions affects the sequence. A clear explanation includes the change and its practical consequence rather than a list of unrelated events.

workedExample.prompt: Describe studying at a different library after moving.
steps: State “引っ越してから、駅の近くの図書館を使っています。”
Explain the meaning: since moving, the speaker has been using the library near the station.

misconception.correction: It can also mark a starting point or sequence, depending on the construction.

questions.hint: The て-form links the completed event to what follows.

questions.prompt: How would you say “before going to school”?
questions.hint: Use dictionary form before 前に.
checkpoints: Places 前に after the verb

modules.title: Propose a small response to a wider issue
modules.focus: Global contexts: explain purpose and evaluate outcomes.
explanation: A proposal should name an action, a purpose and a realistic constraint. “ごみを減らすために” means “in order to reduce rubbish”. The phrase identifies an intention; it does not prove that the action achieved the reduction.

For a fictional reusable-cup trial, distinguish cups distributed from disposable cups avoided. Cleaning, participation and replacement rates affect the outcome. Compare similar periods and consider other changes. This keeps a persuasive argument connected to evidence rather than presenting an imagined success as a result.

workedExample.prompt: Propose a fictional school cup-return scheme.
steps: Write “ごみを減らすために、繰り返し使えるコップを導入したいです。”
Explain that you would like to introduce reusable cups to reduce rubbish, then specify that cleaning arrangements must be checked.

misconception.claim: Stating a purpose demonstrates the result.
misconception.correction: A purpose is an intention; measured outcomes require separate evidence.

questions.prompt: What does ために express in the proposal?
questions.hint: Look at the goal before it.
questions.answer: Purpose: in order to reduce rubbish.
checkpoints: Does not claim a completed result

questions.prompt: What should be measured to evaluate the scheme?
questions.hint: Compare the relevant outcome over similar periods.
questions.answer: Counts of disposable cups used, with records of reusable-cup returns and cleaning, before and during the trial.
